paper_title: Efficient Ensemble for Fine-tuning Language Models on Multiple Datasets
caption: This figure compares the error rate (one average minus test accuracy), computation cost, and GPU memory across our approach and baselines, for fine-tuning Llama-3-8B on ten NLP tasks with QAdapter.

model_annotations.English: The bar chart, titled "QAdapter", illustrates the GPU memory usage across various model fine-tuning methods. The horizontal axis contains the categories, displaying angled text labels without an overarching axis title. The vertical value axis is labeled "GPU Memory (GB)" and employs a linear scale with a visible numeric range from 0 to 60, featuring tick marks and faint horizontal grid lines at intervals of 20, though the plotted data extends upwards to approximately 75. The chart displays six individual vertical bars representing the different methods. The first five categories are colored orange and are arranged from left to right in descending order of their values: "Full FT" is the tallest bar on the chart at approximately 73 GB, followed by "MTL-FT" at roughly 43 GB, "TAG" at about 19 GB, "Adapter" at approximately 17 GB, and "QAdapter", which is the shortest bar at approximately 9 GB. The final category on the right, labeled "Ours", breaks the preceding descending sort order and is visually emphasized. Its bar is colored green instead of orange, indicating a value of approximately 19 GB, and its corresponding x-axis label is printed in a bold, enlarged typeface.
model_annotations.German: This bar chart, titled "QAdapter," illustrates the GPU memory required by various fine-tuning methods. The horizontal axis contains the categorical variables representing different approaches, with labels rotated diagonally: Full FT, MTL-FT, TAG, Adapter, QAdapter, and Ours. There is no explicit label for the horizontal axis. The vertical axis is a linear value axis labeled "GPU Memory (GB)", ranging from 0 to slightly above 70, with numeric tick labels and corresponding light gray horizontal gridlines positioned at intervals of 20. The chart displays six vertical bars. The first five bars are colored orange and are visually sorted in descending order of height from left to right. The tallest bar is "Full FT," reaching an approximate value of 73 GB. It is followed by "MTL-FT" at roughly 43 GB, "TAG" at about 19 GB, "Adapter" at nearly 17 GB, and the shortest bar, "QAdapter," at approximately 8 GB. The final bar on the right, representing the category "Ours," has an approximate value of 19 GB. This final category is visually emphasized in two ways: its bar is colored green instead of orange, and its corresponding label on the horizontal axis is printed in bold text.
